HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE DUPPALA VENKATA RAMANA W.P.Nos.11157,12299, 15738, 20082 of 2009, 3969 of 2012  and  C.C No.2711 of 2022 in W.P.No.11157 of 2009 COMMON ORDER:
With the consent of all the learned counsel all these writ petitions are taken up together.

2. Writ Petition No.11157 of 2009 is filed by five writ petitioners questioning the action of the respondents in interfering with their peaceful possession and enjoyment of the five plots of land situated in Sy.No.149 of Pernamitta Village, Santanutalapadu Mandal, Prakasam District.
3. A counter was filed on behalf of the respondents, wherein it is stated that the land was acquired under Award No.111 of 1982 and later it was allotted to homeless poor people under pattas.
Thereafter, W.P.No.3969 of 2012 was filed by five writ petitioners questioning the action of the respondents in interfering with their possession and also questioning the acquisition of the land.

They prayed for a direction to set aside the Award No.111 of 1982.
4.
W.P.No.12299 of 2009 was filed by 12 petitioners against the official respondents initially.
They also claimed to have purchased the land in Sy.No.149, 150, 153 etc., and claim to be in clear possession.
The implead petitioners, who have come on record, state that they have been allotted pattas by the Government for the land.
The writ petitioners have questioned the entire procedure that is adopted in this case also, including the Award.

5. W.P.No.20082 of 2009 is filed by a single individual, claiming to be an owner, challenging the action of the Executive Engineering, Nagarajuna Sagar Canal, in issuing NOC to the Tahsildar for grant of house sites to the landless poor.

He also raises the issue that the land in Sy.No.149, 150, 153,
118 of Pernametta village, which was meant for excavation of Nagarjunasagar canal was not acquired at all and that the consequential allotment etc., is contrary to law.

He claims to be the owner of plot of land in Sy.No.153.
6.

Writ Petition No.15738 of 2001 is filed by three petitioners for a direction against the respondents from interfering with their peaceful possession and enjoyment of the lands in Sy.No.153 of Pernametta village.

They are the plot owners, who also questioned the allotment of land to third K. Padmavathi, vs A.S. Dinesh Kumar I.A.S. on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35846089/

sentences.text:
7. The State has filed its counter and it is relying upon the Award No.111 of 1982, said to have been passed on 16.03.1982.
8.
This Court has heard all the counsel and the learned Government Pleader for the Land Acquisition.

In view of the fact that the petitioners have raised an issue that there was never any complete land acquisition, learned Government Pleader was given an opportunity of securing and filing the entire record pertaining to acquisition of lands in all these survey numbers and also the Award No.111 of 1982, dated 16.03.1982.

Learned Government Pleader after obtaining instruments submits that there is absolutely no record available except the draft Award to show that the lands in these survey numbers have actually been acquired by following the procedure stipulated under the Land Acquisition Act.
9. Matters were specifically reopened for hearing.
It was again clarified by the respondent that there is no proof to show that an Award was actually passed.

Even earlier in W.P.No.12299 of 2009 when an application was filed to direct the respondents 1 and 2 to produce the records relating to land acquisition vide Award No.111 of 1982, learned single Judge held since rule nisi has already been issued no separate order for production of documents is necessary.

The fact remains that even after an opportunity was given, absolutely no proof was filed to show that the procedure under the land acquisition was initiated and followed leading to the passing of the Award and the vesting of the land in the Government.

The contentions of the learned counsel for the petitioners are that the alignment of the Nagarjuna Sagar canal itself has been changed and therefore the Government did not go ahead with the land acquisition.
It is asserted and stated more than once that the land was never acquired and the compensation etc., was never paid as the canal alignment itself was changed.

Despite all these opportunities the State could not in any manner support its contentions that the land was in fact acquired; that an Award was passed; that it is vested in the State and that consequently they could also allot the land to the unofficial respondents, who were impleaded, in some of the writ petitions.
In the absence of any proof this Court has to hold that the respondent State failed to prove its right, title or possession over the subject lands.
The procedure for land acquisition is a long drawn procedure and if such a procedure has actually taken place, the State would be in possession of records to justify its stand.
The absence of any record leads this Court to an irresistible conclusion, by drawing an adverse inference, that the State does not have any title or possession over the subject lands.
The assertion of the writ petitioners is that they are in possession is also a factor in their favour.
The consequential allotments said to have been made are also held to be bad in law.
10. The Writ Petitions are, therefore, allowed and all the prayers are granted.
Since there is no record filed to show that an Award was in fact passed, it is declared that the respondent-State cannot rely upon the so called Award No.111 of 1982.

11. With regard to the Contempt Case, it is filed in 2022 alleging that the order, dated 10.06.2009,
passed in W.P.No.11157 of 2009 is not complied with.
The alleged contemptuous act relates to the grant of pattas in 2008 and 2009.
But the contempt application is filed in 2022.

This delay itself is a K. Padmavathi, vs A.S. Dinesh Kumar I.A.S. on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35846089/
2 ground to reject the same.

sentences.text: The contempt should have been filed within one year.
As the land was never acquired as per law, the Government could not issue any pattas to third parties.
Hence, no purpose will be served in keeping the C.C.No.2711 of 2022 pending.
Accordingly, the Contempt Case is closed.
No costs.
12. As a sequel thereto, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in these Writ Petitions shall stand closed.
